introduction.definition: A flare stack safely burns hydrocarbon gas released by relief valves, blowdown and upsets. Gas passes a water-seal drum (stopping flashback and air ingress), rises up the riser to the tip where continuous pilots ignite it; steam injected at the tip entrains air for smokeless burning. Its height limits radiation at grade.
applications: Refineries, petrochemical plants and gas processing
key_points: Water seal + purge prevent air ingress

temperature.title: Radiation sets the stack height
temperature.description: A flare safely burns gas released by relief valves and blowdown. Its height and location are set so thermal radiation at grade stays within limits (e.g. ≈ 1.58 kW/m² for continuous exposure of personnel, higher for short emergency exposure — API 521, verify edition). Steam (or air) injected at the tip mixes air into the flame for smokeless burning; continuous pilots guarantee ignition; the water seal and purge gas with a molecular seal stop air entering and flashback.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Flare Stack.
Monitor pilots, steam, flame (camera).
Check seal level and purge flow.
Inspect tip and pilots at turnaround.
Watch for smoking flare: black smoke. Common cause: too little steam.
Watch for pilot out: flame-out alarm. Common cause: fuel / wind.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
